statement: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Two angles that lie between the parallel lines and on the same side of the transversal measure $(3x + 15)^\circ$ and $(2x + 5)^\circ$. What is the value of $x$?

choices.misconception: I thought the two angles add to $90^\circ$, so I solved $5x + 20 = 90$.
I thought the two angles add to $360^\circ$, so I solved $5x + 20 = 360$.
I solved $5x + 20 = 180$ correctly but then reported the angle $3(32) + 15 = 111$ instead of $x$.

hints: Same-side interior angles have a fixed sum.
When the lines are parallel, these two angles are supplementary, so their measures add to $180^\circ$.

solutions.reliable: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, the interior angles on the same side of the transversal are supplementary. So $(3x + 15) + (2x + 5) = 180$, which gives $5x + 20 = 180$, $5x = 160$ and $x = 32$. Check: the angles are $111^\circ$ and $69^\circ$, which add to $180^\circ$.
